questions.stem: Register is best defined as

options.text: a list of names kept by a school office
the variety of language that fits a particular situation, field and audience
any difficult word, whatever the situation

questions.explanation: Register is language fitted to the situation: what is going on, who is speaking to whom, and whether the channel is speech or writing. A class register is a different sense of the word, and difficulty alone does not make a register.

distractorRationale.a: That is the everyday school meaning of register, not the linguistic one tested here
distractorRationale.c: Hard words appear in every field; the field, not the difficulty, defines the register
distractorRationale.d: Punctuation is a separate topic

questions.stem: The words plaintiff, affidavit, injunction and adjournment belong to the register of
questions.explanation: A plaintiff brings a civil case, an affidavit is a sworn statement, an injunction is a court order, and adjournment is the postponement of a hearing. The shared activity is the courtroom, so the field is law.

distractorRationale.a: Medical clusters use diagnosis, prescription, incision — none of these four
distractorRationale.c: Agriculture uses fallow, irrigation, harvest
distractorRationale.d: Sports uses offside, penalty, referee

questions.stem: The words diagnosis, prescription, contagious and incision belong to the register of
questions.explanation: Diagnosis names a condition, a prescription orders treatment, contagious describes infection, and an incision is a surgical cut. The shared activity is clinical practice, so the field is medicine.

distractorRationale.a: Journalism uses by-line, headline, scoop, deadline
distractorRationale.b: ICT uses browser, malware, bandwidth, login
distractorRationale.d: Law uses plaintiff, affidavit, counsel — incision is not a legal word

questions.stem: The magistrate asked counsel to produce a sworn written statement. The register word for that statement is
questions.explanation: An affidavit is a written statement sworn before an authorised officer, which is exactly what a magistrate would ask counsel to produce. The other three words belong to medicine, journalism and ICT.

questions.stem: "The striker was ruled _____ because he was ahead of the last defender when the ball was played." Choose the correct register word.
questions.explanation: The sentence is already in sports register: striker, defender, ball. The rule that a player is illegally ahead of the defence is offside. Staying inside the field the sentence has chosen is the whole method.

distractorRationale.a: Law — postponing a hearing
distractorRationale.c: Agriculture — unsown land
distractorRationale.d: Medicine — able to spread infection

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Lexis and Structure

questions.stem: Which word is the odd one out in this cluster: editor, correspondent, scoop, irrigation, deadline?
questions.explanation: Editor, correspondent, scoop and deadline are journalism. Irrigation is watering crops, which belongs to agriculture. The odd-one-out method is the cluster question in reverse: four words share a field, one does not.

distractorRationale.a: A newsroom role — journalism
distractorRationale.b: A reporter abroad or in the field — journalism
distractorRationale.d: The time a story must be filed — journalism

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Lexis and Structure

questions.stem: A computer-lab notice reads: "Do not download files from unknown sites; they may contain _____." The best register word is
questions.explanation: Download and unknown sites place the sentence in ICT. Malware is harmful software, which is exactly what such a warning is about. Pesticide, injunction and equaliser are accurate words in agriculture, law and sports, and therefore wrong here.

distractorRationale.a: Agriculture — a chemical that kills pests
distractorRationale.c: Law — a court order to stop an action
distractorRationale.d: Sports — a goal that levels the score
